summary: A tight, fast two-player duel where you draft cards from a shifting pyramid, racing to build a stronger civilization across three ages while watching your opponent's military and science tracks like a hawk. Games can end abruptly via military conquest or a science victory long before the normal point-count finish, which keeps every pick tense.
praised: Extremely tight, tense two-player experience with constant meaningful decisions
Elegant card-drafting mechanism where visibility and access to cards matters as much as the cards themselves
Fast to teach and play (30 minutes) yet very deep strategically
Multiple viable paths to victory (military, science, civilian points) create real tension
High replayability due to variable setup and interaction between paths
criticised: Strictly two-player only, no way to scale up or down
Sudden-death military/science wins can feel abrupt or swingy if one path snowballs unnoticed
Some card/wonder combinations are considered stronger than others, leading to perceived imbalance
Can feel overwhelming for newer players tracking multiple resource and progress tracks at once

interaction.kind: card denial and racing on shared tracks

scoring.why: Points come from civilian buildings, science sets, commerce, and wonders, but the game is often decided outright before scoring by a military or scientific sudden-death win.
